extracted.intended_audience: BBC journalists, editors, producers and other BBC content-makers worldwide
extracted.subtask_description: The BBC's official editorial standards covering values, principles and mandatory referral points for producing and publishing BBC content across all platforms and territories.

rubrics_metrics.name: 1: The BBC's Editorial Standards
rubrics_metrics.description: The Editorial Guidelines set the BBC's editorial values and standards and apply to all BBC content wherever in the world it is broadcast or published.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Section includes: Introduction; The BBC's Editorial Values; How to use the Guidelines. Provides the overarching framework and editorial values that inform all subsequent topic-specific guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: 2: Impartiality
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance on impartiality including introduction and principles governing balance and neutrality in BBC content.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Subsections: Introduction and Principles; Mandatory Referrals; Guidelines. Covers expectations for impartial reporting, when issues must be referred, and practical guidance on applying impartiality principles.

rubrics_metrics.name: 3: Accuracy
rubrics_metrics.description: Standards and principles for ensuring accuracy in BBC reporting and content.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Subsections: Introduction and Principles; Mandatory Referrals; Guidelines. Sets out accuracy expectations, error correction responsibilities and referral triggers where accuracy concerns arise.

rubrics_metrics.name: 4: Conflicts of Interest
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance on identifying and managing conflicts of interest among BBC staff and contributors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Subsections: Introduction and Principles; Mandatory Referrals; Guidelines. Explains what counts as a conflict, required disclosures and referral/management processes.

rubrics_metrics.name: 5: Harm and Offence
rubrics_metrics.description: Standards for minimising harm and avoiding unjustified offence in content.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Subsections: Introduction and Principles; Mandatory Referrals; Guidelines. Covers assessment of potential harm/offence, editorial judgement and mandatory referral requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: 6: Fairness
rubrics_metrics.description: Principles and practical guidance to ensure fairness in treatment of people and subjects in BBC content.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Subsections: Introduction and Principles; Mandatory Referrals; Guidelines. Addresses fair representation, giving subjects opportunity to respond and related referral points.

rubrics_metrics.name: 7: Privacy
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance on respecting individuals' privacy when gathering and presenting BBC content.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Subsections: Introduction and Principles; Mandatory Referrals; Guidelines. Sets out privacy thresholds, lawful/ethical considerations and when to escalate decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: 8: Crime and Anti-social Behaviour
rubrics_metrics.description: Standards for reporting crime and anti-social behaviour responsibly and legally.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Subsections: Introduction and Principles; Mandatory Referrals; Guidelines. Includes guidance on naming suspects, reporting live incidents, and mandatory referral triggers.

rubrics_metrics.name: 9: Children and Young People as Contributors
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules and principles governing the participation of children and young people in BBC content.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Subsections: Introduction and Principles; Mandatory Referrals; Guidelines. Covers consent, safeguarding, appropriate treatment and required referrals.

rubrics_metrics.name: 10: Politics and Public Policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Editorial guidance for covering politics and public policy matters impartially and accurately.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Subsections: Introduction and Principles; Mandatory Referrals; Guidelines. Addresses political balance, party politics, elections, and when issues must be escalated.

rubrics_metrics.name: 11: Statistics, Polls, Data and Surveys
rubrics_metrics.description: Standards for using and presenting statistics, polls, data and survey results.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Subsections: Introduction and Principles; Mandatory Referrals; Guidelines. Covers verification, presentation clarity, caveats and referral points for contested or complex data.

rubrics_metrics.name: 12: War, Terror and Extreme Violence, Disaster and Disorder
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance on reporting war, terrorism, extreme violence, disasters and disorder with sensitivity and accuracy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Subsections: Introduction and Principles; Mandatory Referrals; Guidelines. Addresses safety of contributors, graphic content, verification in conflict zones and mandatory escalation.

rubrics_metrics.name: 13: Use of BBC Content after Publication or Broadcast
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules governing how BBC content may be reused, shared or repurposed after initial publication or broadcast.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Subsections: Introduction and Principles; Mandatory Referrals; Guidelines. Sets expectations for reuse permissions, attribution, takedowns and referral procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: 14: Religious Content
rubrics_metrics.description: Principles and guidance for handling religious content and coverage of faith-related matters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Subsections: Introduction; Principles; Guidelines. Focuses on respect, accuracy, context and appropriate treatment of religious belief and communities.

rubrics_metrics.name: 15: Independence from Commercial and other External Interests
rubrics_metrics.description: Standards to preserve editorial independence from commercial and external influences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Subsections: Introduction and Principles; Mandatory Referrals; Guidelines. Explains boundaries between editorial content and commercial/third-party interests, and when to escalate potential breaches.

rubrics_metrics.name: 16: External Relationships, including Commercial Relationships, and Financing
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance on managing external relationships, commercial partnerships and financing arrangements that could affect BBC content.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Subsections: Introduction and Principles; Mandatory Referrals; Guidelines. Covers transparency, conflicts, sponsorship, and referral/approval processes.

rubrics_metrics.name: 17: Competitions, Votes and Interactivity
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules and principles for running competitions, audience votes and interactive content.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Subsections: Introduction and Principles; Mandatory Referrals; Guidelines. Includes fairness, legality, moderation and escalation/referral requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: 18: The Law
rubrics_metrics.description: Legal considerations applicable to BBC content, including mandatory referral points and principal legal considerations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Subsections: Introduction and Mandatory Referrals; General; Principal Legal Considerations. Sets out legal risks, compliance expectations and when legal advice/referral is required.
